uncertain_sources: The early kinetic-theory passage contains recognition noise; the chapter preserves its methodological role and collision-rate outline without inventing a detailed wall-pressure calculation that the lecture does not complete.

The lecture verbally reverses the broadening of the canonical distribution with temperature while answering a monotonicity question; the chapter corrects the direction and states the stable-system relation between the entropy derivative and heat capacity.

The compressed board discussion from Helmholtz free energy to the log-partition-function pressure formula is recognition-noisy; the chapter carries the sign directly from dE equals minus P dV and the preceding calculus lemma.
The classical ideal-gas integral suppresses the phase-space cell; the chapter restores h to the power 3N so the partition function is dimensionless while retaining the lecture's volume derivative.
The lecture uses adiabatic for both slow and insulated change; the chapter distinguishes thermal insulation from quasistatic reversibility and explains why the combined process is isentropic.
The lecture initially calls the total derivative of sample energy with temperature a specific heat and later corrects it to heat capacity; the chapter uses the corrected terminology.

The smallness of macroscopic fluctuations is stated through the appearance of Boltzmann's constant; the chapter supplies the extensive scaling that makes the relative fluctuation proportional to one over the square root of N.
